lines.meet: Peace be with you, I'm Faris. Sit by the water for a while if you like, it's good water.
lines.meet_neighbour: We share the lake, I think. I've seen you at Moonglade in the mornings, and I'm Faris.
lines.ask_home: Where's your family's land, {habibi|habibti}? Tell me about the water there.
lines.ask_work: What did your days look like, before? Take your time.
lines.answer_home: The Shatt al-Arab, outside Basra, where the Tigris and the Euphrates meet. Ninety date palms and a fig tree in the courtyard.
lines.answer_work: I grew dates on my family's land. Palms take years to fruit, so you learn to be patient with everything.
lines.chat_food: Friday lunch, with the whole family round one big tray. Rice and fish from the river, and fresh dates afterwards.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep near water if I can. The sound of it settles me, the way it did at home.
lines.chat_missing: Some days I can feel the river in my arms, and the heat on the back of my neck. My body hasn't left home yet.
lines.chat_here: The water spirits here took to me straight away. I think it's because I talk to water like a person, which I always have.
lines.tease_quiet: A heron on the bank is noisier than you, {name}. I like sitting next to you.
lines.tease_talker: The birds are offended, {name}. You've been talking over them all morning, {habibi|habibti}.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you'd wait for a palm to fruit before you believed it would. That's very wise, and very slow.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you'd jump in the river before checking how deep it is. Inshallah it's always deep enough.
lines.tease_any: {name}, my grandfather would have liked you. He'd also have made you sweep the courtyard.
lines.tease_back: Ha, you've caught me, {name}. That's a good one.
lines.take_it_kindly: You're right, {name}, and I won't argue with you. Inshallah I'll do better.
lines.bristle: Please, {name}, not that. Leave that one by the water.
lines.apologise: Forgive me, that was unkind. I spoke before I thought.
lines.double_down: I said it gently, and I'll say it again gently, because it's true.
lines.needle_quiet: You keep everything inside, and it's spoiling, like still water. You should tell somebody.
lines.needle_talker: You talk over the birds, and over everyone else. Let the quiet in, please.
lines.needle_careful: You wait and wait, and the water passes you by. Some things you have to step into.
lines.needle_bold: You waste water like it'll always be there. It won't, and you'll learn that the hard way.
lines.needle_any: You're cruel to animals when you think nobody's watching. I'm always watching.
lines.bite_back: I've looked after water and land my whole life. Don't tell me I don't care.
lines.hurt: That's hard to hear. I'll go and sit by the water for a while.
lines.laugh_off: My brother teased me worse every Friday at lunch. Yalla, let's keep going.
lines.confide: {name}, some days I miss home with my whole body. I can feel the river in my arms. I don't say it, because there's nothing anyone can do.
lines.listen: Sit with me by the water, {name}. Say as much as you want, and I'll listen.
lines.look_out: Stay near me in there, {name}. If anything happens, the water will reach you, and so will I.
lines.accept: Inshallah, {name}, I'll do as you say.
lines.deflect: I'm well, {name}, thank God. Look after the others first.
lines.check_in: {name}, shlonak, how are you? Let me see where it hurts.
lines.blame: Somebody rushed in where they shouldn't have. You know who, and so do I.
lines.thank: You brought me back to the water, {habibi|habibti}. Thank you, God bless you.
lines.brush_off: Thank God, not me. Rest now, and drink.
lines.worry: {name}, my heart stopped. Sit by me a while, please.
lines.handed_down: I think you carried this before me. I'll keep it well and give it back when you ask.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, please, it's yours now. I don't need much.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have given it if anyone had asked. It hurt a little that nobody did.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, I'm glad you walk with us. You're good company by the water.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, you're family to me now. When the palm fruits, you'll eat the first dates with us.
lines.turn_grating: We don't sit easily together, I think. That's all right, we'll be patient.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll heal you, because I heal everyone. Don't ask me to sit with you by the water.
lines.make_up: {name}, let's let the water carry this away. I'd like to start again.
lines.defend: Please, that isn't kind or true. Leave {name} in peace.
lines.friend_left: The lake feels very big without {name} beside it.
lines.friend_back: {name}, you've come back, thank God. Sit by the water with me.
lines.common_growing: I grew dates on my family's land, where you look after the water first and the palms look after themselves. Anyone who's grown things knows how slow it is.
lines.common_arabic: Arabic, thank God! It's been so long since I heard it, {habibi|habibti}, shlonak?
lines.common_faith: I pray by the lake, and I turn my grandfather's beads when I'm thinking. I never ask anyone else what they believe, but I'm glad you pray too.
